text:
devon: Heads-up — Helio Health asks us to classify their workload into GPU tiers before they sign. They have mixed traffic: low-latency chat bursts + nightly bulk embeddings. Need: recommended GPU class, rough # of reserved GPUs, autoscale policy suggestion, and a cost split example for reserved vs burst credits. Anyone free to sketch?
marta: OK — quick Qs: (1) chat concurrency during peak? (2) median tokens per chat vs max? (3) embeddings QPS and vector dims?
sanjay: From the POC logs earlier: chat peak ~220 qps for 30m, median tokens ~40, p95 tokens ~420. Embeddings: steady 120 qps at 1536-dim, nightly batch ~3M vectors over 6 hours.
devon: great, that's what i have for now. Goal is a 3-month reserved commit with burst credits for spikes. They want predictable tail latency <200ms for chat.
marta: For <200ms tail we should recommend H100-class for chat if model is large (70B+), otherwise A100-80GB is fine for 20–33B. Do they plan to use quantized model (4-bit) for embeddings? that changes throughput by ~2–3x.
sanjay: They said they'd prefer open models; engineering team testing a 33B quantized. So assume 4-bit for chat and embeddings.
ops-bot: NOTE: recommended autoscale policy template "reserved-plus-burst":
```
min_replicas: reserved_capacity
scale_up_policy: cpu+queue_depth (fast)
burst_pool: enabled (limited credit per minute)
fallback: lower-capacity quantized-model
```
marta: Sizing sketch (ballpark):
- Chat (33B q4): ~1 reserved GPU (A100x80) handles ~150 qps at p95 <200ms with batching tuned + prefix cache. For 220 qps peak we suggest reserved=2 with burst to 3.
- Embeddings (quantized): 1 GPU (prefer H100 if budget) can do ~250–350 qps depending on batch. For nightly 3M vectors over 6h -> ~140 qps sustained; so 1 GPU reserved with autoscale to 2 for pre/post spikes.
- So commit: reserved 3 GPUs across pools (2 chat, 1 embed) with burst credits for +50% peak.
devon: rough cost model request from finance: show delta reserved vs pay-as-you-go (hosted) for monthly. Can you give a simple calc?
sanjay: quick calc assumptions (strings):
- Reserved GPU monthly cost: $Xk per GPU/mo (we'll put exact in deck)
- Hosted per-token/embedding units: depends on model but assume 0.002/token equivalent and 0.0008/embed-unit.
- Example math: Reserved 3 GPUs -> amortized per-request cost drops ~40–60% vs hosted at current traffic; details need exact rates.
marta: I'll make a small spreadsheet but show a scenario: reserved saves money once sustained load > ~110 qps chat + continuous embeddings. We'll include a sensitivity table (+/- 30% traffic).
devon: Legal/security question: they asked whether reserved capacity is on shared infra or customer-dedicated instances and about KMS for keys in Private. li-legal any blockers?
li-legal: For enterprise commit we can offer Dedicated (customer-isolated) or Private (VPC) depending on requirements. Need the security questionnaire answers in the next 48h. Also note: auditing/kms integration requires architecture doc + SOC artifacts. I'll ping them.
devon: can we include KV warmup / preheat notes? customer worried about cold-start degradations.
marta: Yes — recommend KV preheat window 30–45m before business-critical windows. For startup: pre-create KV cache from sampled prompts and do a warmup script. Example curl to trigger warmup:
```
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.run/generate -d '{"prompt":"seed"}' &
sleep 0.02
done
```
sanjay: Ops note: Also recommend autoscale cooldown 60s and queue-depth based throttling to avoid cascading latency. Set canary fallback to smaller quantized model to maintain availability.
devon: action items — marta draft sizing + cost spreadsheet, sanjay draft autoscale + preheat runbook, li-legal start questionnaire answers. I’ll loop in customer and set review 48h.
marta: got it. I'll attach numbers and 2 scenarios (conservative / aggressive). :thumbsup:
sanjay: I'll add the runbook snippet and a smoke test plan for preheat.
li-legal: I'll send first-pass security answers and required docs list by EOD tomorrow.
devon: thanks all. i'll send the customer the summary and schedule the 1-hr walkthru.
